verdicts.decision_note: The failed attempts being reported as completed mints establish that only confirmed on-chain mints should be recorded and counted.
The client observed two failed ETH attempts being displayed as completed mints.
The freelancer claims failed transactions are no longer registered and only successful transactions are recorded.
After the claimed fix, the client still observed two false NFT records despite the mint not working.
The client confirms that the false mint-derived NFT records were no longer displayed.
The displayed mint number remained inconsistent with the absence of corresponding successful paid mints.
The freelancer claims the wrong-contract issue was corrected and that supply should now be zero with the next mint numbered one.
The client reports an executed USDC mint transaction that the platform counted, despite a separate NFT-display problem.
Concrete on-chain inspection confirmed that the counted USDC mint created token number one and assigned ownership.

execution.observed_behavior: Platform statistics showed one total mint while the interface also said the project was up to mint number 4.

verdicts.decision_note: The supply inconsistency is supported, but owned-NFT and referral-code values belong to other Requirements.
